'''Yakym:''' {{legend0|#E27F7F|50–60%}} {{legend0|#D75D5D|60–70%}} {{legend0|#D72F30|70–80%}} | title = U.S. Representative | before_election = [[Jackie Walorski]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Rudy Yakym]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{Elections in Indiana sidebar}} The '''2022 Indiana's 2nd congressional district special election''' was a special election to choose a new member of the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House of Representatives]]. The seat became vacant after incumbent Congresswoman [[Jackie Walorski]] died in a traffic collision on August 3, 2022.{{cite news|last=Karni|first=Annie|date=August 3, 2022|title=Jackie Walorski, Indiana congresswoman, is dead at 58|work=[[The New York Times]]|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/08/03/us/politics/jackie-walorski.html|url-status=live|access-date=August 3, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220803215131/https://www.nytimes.com/2022/08/03/us/politics/jackie-walorski.html|archive-date=August 3, 2022}}{{cite news|last1=Zanona|first1=Melanie|last2=Foran|first2=Clare|date=August 3, 2022|title=Indiana Republican Rep. Jackie Walorski dies in car accident that also killed 2 staffers|work=[[CNN]]|url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/08/03/politics/jackie-walorski-died-indiana-republican|url-status=live|access-date=August 3, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220803224507/https://www.cnn.com/2022/08/03/politics/jackie-walorski-died-indiana-republican|archive-date=August 3, 2022}} In accordance with Title 3, Article 10, of the [[Indiana Code]], a special election must be held for any U.S. House vacancy that occurs more than 74 days before the next general election.{{cite web|title=Indiana Code, Title 3|url=http://iga.in.gov/legislative/laws/2021/ic/titles/003#3-10-8-1|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220510075705/http://iga.in.gov/legislative/laws/2021/ic/titles/003|archive-date=May 10, 2022|access-date=August 3, 2022|website=[[Indiana General Assembly]]}} On August 9, Governor [[Eric Holcomb]] announced the special election was to be held concurrently with the general election on November 8.{{cite news|last=Lange|first=Kaitlin|date=August 9, 2022|title=Gov. Holcomb calls special election to fill Rep. Walorski's seat|work=[[The Indianapolis Star]]|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/news/politics/2022/08/09/indiana-gov-holcomb-special-election-jackie-warloski-seat-congresswoman-death/65397613007/|url-status=live|access-date=August 9, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220810194137/https://www.indystar.com/story/news/politics/2022/08/09/indiana-gov-holcomb-special-election-jackie-warloski-seat-congresswoman-death/65397613007/|archive-date=August 10, 2022}} Parties held caucuses to nominate their candidates for the election; they had until August 26 to do so.{{cite news|last=Chapman|first=Lauren|date=August 9, 2022|title=Holcomb calls special election for Walorski's second congressional district seat|work=[[WFIU]]|url=https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/holcomb-calls-special-election-for-walorskis-second-congressional-district-seat.php|url-status=live|access-date=August 9, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220812225905/https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/holcomb-calls-special-election-for-walorskis-second-congressional-district-seat.php|archive-date=August 12, 2022}} Since the congressional district boundaries set in [[2020 United States redistricting cycle|the 2020 redistricting cycle]] went into effect on January 3, 2023, the special election was conducted under the old district lines whereas [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Indiana#District 2|the regular election]] on the same date was conducted under the new district lines. == Republican caucus == The [[Indiana Republican Party]] held its nominating caucus in [[Mishawaka, Indiana|Mishawaka]] on August 20.{{cite news|last=Smith|first=Casey|date=August 9, 2022|title=Indiana governor calls special election to replace U.S. Rep. Jackie Walorski|work=[[States Newsroom|Indiana Capital Chronicle]]|publisher=[[Ball State University#Ball State Daily News|Ball State Daily News]]|url=https://www.ballstatedailynews.com/article/2022/08/news-indianacaptialchronicle-indiana-governor-calls-special-election-to-replace-u-s-rep-jackie-walorski|url-status=live|access-date=August 9, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220812230640/https://www.ballstatedailynews.com/article/2022/08/news-indianacaptialchronicle-indiana-governor-calls-special-election-to-replace-u-s-rep-jackie-walorski|archive-date=August 12, 2022}} Out of approximately 500 precinct committee members who were eligible to vote,{{cite news|date=August 20, 2022|title=Rudy Yakym gets GOP nod to replace late U.S. Rep. Walorski|agency=[[Associated Press]]|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/rudy-yakym-gets-gop-nod-to-replace-late-us-rep-walorski/2022/08/20/e6468494-20b4-11ed-9ce6-68253bd31864_story.html|url-status=live|access-date=August 20, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220823001243/https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/rudy-yakym-gets-gop-nod-to-replace-late-us-rep-walorski/2022/08/20/e6468494-20b4-11ed-9ce6-68253bd31864_story.html|archive-date=August 23, 2022}} about 375 were present at the caucus.{{cite news|last=Lanich|first=Carley|date=August 20, 2022|title=Rudy Yakym, candidate endorsed by Jackie Walorski's husband, picked in Indiana GOP caucus|work=[[South Bend Tribune]]|url=https://www.southbendtribune.com/story/news/politics/2022/08/20/rudy-yakym-tapped-as-indiana-gop-nominee-for-2nd-congressional-district-jackie-walorski/65411596007/|url-status=live|access-date=August 23, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220823002655/https://www.southbendtribune.com/story/news/politics/2022/08/20/rudy-yakym-tapped-as-indiana-gop-nominee-for-2nd-congressional-district-jackie-walorski/65411596007/|archive-date=August 23, 2022}} The number of votes received by each candidate was not made public; [[Indiana Republican Party]] chair Kyle Hupfer said in a statement that [[Rudy Yakym]] received a majority of votes in the first round of balloting and was thus selected to replace Walorski as the Republican nominee in [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Indiana#District 2|the 2022 regular election]]. Subsequently, Yakym also won the nomination for the special election by voice vote. === Candidates === ==== Nominee ==== *[[Rudy Yakym]], [[supply chain management]] executive and former finance
